text:
Sen. Bill Cunningham casts affirmative vote on HB0111 to fund Illinois Department of Revenue
D. M. Cotton
Sen. Bill Cunningham (D-18th) supported HB0111 with a Yes vote during the 104th General Assembly on May 31, 2026, the Illinois Senate reports; the legislation passed with a 37-21 vote.
The bill's full text states: "$FY 2027 BUDGET."
Below is a summary and interpretation of the bill's content for clarification purposes.
This legislation allocates $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Illinois Department of Revenue to cover regular and contingent expenses for fiscal year 2026 and sets an effective date of July 1, 2025.
The legislative action on HB0111 was recorded as 'Third Reading - Passed'.
Cunningham completed his Bachelor of Arts at the University of Illinois, Chicago in 1990.
He joined the Illinois State Senate as a Democrat in 2013, representing the 18th Senate District after succeeding Edward Maloney.
Illinois bills progress through a multi-step legislative process involving introduction in either chamber, committee deliberations, floor debate, and votes in both houses, before reaching the governor for approval or veto. The General Assembly operates on a two-year cycle, introducing thousands of bills each session, although only a select number become law.
